resolution: Diagnosed and fixed the stair-top invisible-wall stick from the user's RJIT_STAIRLOG capture. The smoking gun: at a staircase crest (x~81, y=3.2) the player held full forward intent yet froze, with rectpush=0 and hfcancel=false but the new integ/clamp columns showing the integrator produce integ=(2.40,..) while clampUphillSurfaceSpeed scaled it to clamp=(0.01,..). Root cause is a positive-feedback death spiral in that clamp: it estimated slope as a finite difference dividing the next-cell height rise by the player's own displacement (horizontal_speed*dt), so as the clamp slowed the player the same tiny crest lip read as an ever-steeper slope and clamped harder until fully pinned. Fixed by capping uphill speed via the surface gradient (up-normal): admissible horizontal = max_surface_speed*normal_y, which equals the old closed form on a uniform slope but is velocity-independent so the loop can't form and never collapses to zero. User confirmed the in-game fix works. Also ruled out the user's hidden-wall-piece hypothesis (a solid rect would show nonzero rectpush). no-V8 loader builds clean; game-physics 39/40, the one red (hollow-ramp-slab rect step-up surface_speed) predates this work.
